transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-08
Time: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Evan Ruiz (BlueMetric CTO), Priya Desai (Head of ML), Sam Torres (SRE), Lena Wu (Finance)

Auto-generated Summary:
Quick operational QBR-style check-in focusing on usage spikes from last month, cost anomalies for embedding-heavy endpoints, reliability concerns during batch jobs, and a pilot proposal for Dedicated capacity with a short benchmark plan. Action items and concrete next steps agreed.

Topics:
- Last 30-day usage & cost anomalies
- Latency spikes during scheduled batch reranks
- Dedicated vs Hosted pilot tradeoffs (SLA, data isolation, cost predictability)
- Security checklist: SOC2, SAML, audit logs, KMS
- Roadmap alignment and pilot success criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: All right, hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off, uh, quick agenda — usage, cost, reliability and then a proposed pilot. Maya and I will go through a couple numbers. Evan, Priya, Sam, Lena, thanks for making time.

[01:10] Evan Ruiz: Yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it. Quick note from our side, uh, last month we saw an unexpected 3x spike on the embedding endpoint which drove the bill up. We think it was the nightly rerank job that escalated, but need to confirm exact traces.

[02:05] Maya Chen: Got it. When you say embedding endpoint, is that the batched embedding job for search vectors or the near-real-time user embeddings?

[02:22] Priya Desai: It's the nightly job, batched, we re-embed product descriptions overnight, about 12 million tokens total in the window. Usually runs at 2am but on that date it overlapped with some feature rollout and the concurrency jumped.

[03:05] Sam Torres: There were some autoscale delays too. We saw queueing on our side so the requests got retried, which amplified the throughput — I think that created the nested retries.

[03:40] Jordan Patel: That tracks. Two levers we usually recommend — scheduled off-peak windows for big batches + Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput. Dedicated will give you pinned GPU pools and avoids noisy neighbor issues. But it comes with a committed cost.

[04:05] Lena Wu: Right, from finance perspective we like predictability. We just need clear unit economics. Can you show a projection for committed vs. pay-as-you-go?

[04:30] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll do a side-by-side. Also there are mid-ground options — reserved burst capacity and autoscale policies tuned to batch windows. We can run a short pilot and capture per-token cost and latency P95.

[05:12] Evan Ruiz: What's the typical SLO for Dedicated vs Hosted? We saw P95s spike to 2.3s on the rerank endpoints. Our target is sub-1s for interactive calls and sub-5s for nightly jobs.

[05:45] Maya Chen: Hosted aims for low latency but shared pools can see variance. Dedicated gives you SLA backed latency bands and consistent P95s. We'll also recommend batching and KV cache tuning for your workload. Note: KV cache was mis-typed in some of our earlier notes as K V cash, apologies in the docs.

[06:30] Priya Desai: On quality, we can't quantize too aggressively. Some of our rerank models require FP16 to avoid accuracy regression. Are you running quantization recommendations per-model?

[07:02] Jordan Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles per model and sequence length. For sensitive rerank models we often keep FP16 or Q4x with a short eval to catch regressions. We'll include quality guardrails in the pilot.

[08:10] Sam Torres: Security questions — we need SAML/SSO, audit logs, KMS integration and possible VPC peering for Private deployment. Do you support customer-managed KMS?

[08:40] Maya Chen: Yes — for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. Hosted supports envelope encryption and we can integrate with your KMS for key rotation if needed. We'll share our SOC 2 and network diagrams.

[09:20] Evan Ruiz: Great. Can you also provide sample audit log retention options? Compliance wants 18 months, so we need to confirm retention policies and export hooks.

[09:45] Jordan Patel: We'll include that in the security packet. Typical retention tiers are 90 days in Console by default, with add-on longer retention for enterprise packages. We'll send options.

[10:20] Priya Desai: On performance, we want to run a small 2-week benchmark: serve 10k concurrent embedding requests at our typical seq distribution and a parallel rerank stream. We want latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, and model quality metrics.

[11:05] Maya Chen: Sounds good. We'll supply benchmark scripts and a runner that you can run from your infra. We'll ask for representative prompt sets and sequence length histograms.

[12:10] Sam Torres: About VPC — our network team needs to schedule a peering window. Also we prefer pilot to use private endpoints to avoid blowing up production secrets in test traffic.

[12:40] Jordan Patel: We can isolate pilot traffic. For Dedicated pilot we typically provision a small pool and give you access to metrics in Console. We'll enable tracing hooks so you can map requests to model invocations.

[13:30] Lena Wu: On pricing structure, can you outline how token pricing + reserved capacity interacts? We want to know break-even point vs pay-as-you-go.

[14:05] Maya Chen: We'll provide a cost model. Example: if you commit to X GPU-hours per month the unit cost per token drops by Y%. We'll include a break-even chart based on your current 30-day usage.

[15:00] Evan Ruiz: Are there any known limitations around quantized models and certain attention patterns — for example long context reranks at 8k tokens?

[15:30] Maya Chen: For long contexts, kernel selection matters. Our runtime picks kernels optimized for sequence length but some quantization modes behave worse at extended sequences. We'll test your 8k flows in the pilot.

[16:05] Priya Desai: Ok — let's talk success criteria for the pilot. From BlueMetric side: 1) consistent p95 below 1.2s for interactive routes, 2) nightly rerank cost reduced by 25% (or at least predictable), 3) no data exfil risk and SAML integration.

[16:45] Jordan Patel: That's concrete and great. From Redwood we'll add: benchmark scripts run, quality regressions under threshold (we'll define exact eval pass/fail), and to validate autoscale behavior under your traffic spike patterns.

[17:30] Evan Ruiz: Timeline idea — pilot kickoff week of 5/25, two weeks of benchmarking, then review. Can you commit to deliverables before then?

[17:50] Jordan Patel: Yes — Maya will push scripts by 5/12, I'll send pricing and SOW by 5/15, you confirm prompt sets by 5/11 and network peering windows by 5/13; then we can target 5/25 kickoff.

[18:20] Priya Desai: Slight clarification on the prompt sets — we'll send two representative sets: interactive user queries and nightly rerank prompts. Also note we have GDPR-loc data residency concerns for EU users.

[18:55] Maya Chen: For data residency we can route EU traffic to region-specific pools and ensure logs are retained per-region. We'll flag any export hooks that cross regions.

[19:30] Sam Torres: One more ops note — our oncall team wants runbooks for fallback behaviors. If Dedicated pool goes unhealthy, what's the automatic fallback?

[19:50] Jordan Patel: Redwood supports automatic model variant fallback and region fallback. We can configure canary rollouts and automatic routing to hosted backups. We'll document exactly what happens and surface it in Console runbook entries.

[20:25] Evan Ruiz: Any limitations on SDKs or agent integrations? We're using internal Python SDK and a small node microservice.

[20:45] Maya Chen: SDKs are supported for both — we have Python, Node, and REST. There was a minor serialization quirk with older Node client versions, but we'll send the compatibility matrix.

[21:30] Priya Desai: Regarding quality monitoring, can we tie eval alerts to specific prompt sets? We want alerts if rerank NDCG drops more than 1.5%.

[21:50] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Optimize supports prompt-set linked quality monitoring and regression alerts. We'll help you onboard the evals and set thresholds.

[22:30] Jordan Patel: Cool. Let's do a quick recap of action items and owners.

[23:00] (recap) Jordan Patel: Jordan will send pricing and SOW by 5/15. Maya will send benchmark scripts + compatibility matrix by 5/12. BlueMetric (Priya) will provide prompt sets and token distributions by 5/11. Sam to confirm VPC peering window by 5/13.

[24:20] Lena Wu: From finance, we'll review the SOW and circle back on budget approvals.

[24:40] Evan Ruiz: Also to add — we'll run an internal dry-run of the nightly job to capture where retries are happening and share logs with Maya.

[25:05] Maya Chen: Please scrub any PII before sharing logs; we can accept sanitized traces. We'll also provide a redact checklist.

[25:40] Priya Desai: Quick question — do you have recommended model variants for rerank that balance cost and quality?

[26:00] Maya Chen: We'll propose two — a high-fidelity FP16 variant and a cost-optimized Q4x. We'll include historical eval comparisons.

[27:15] Sam Torres: Is there support for canary deploys across model versions for rollback?

[27:35] Jordan Patel: Yes we support canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback policies. We'll show an example config.

[28:10] Evan Ruiz: Any red flags from Redwood side for this pilot?

[28:20] Maya Chen: Just clarity on prompt sets and the VPC window. The rest looks straightforward. We might note slight quality variance for extreme sequence lengths but we'll catch it in the benchmark.

[29:00] Priya Desai: Ok great. On the security packet — could you include SOC2 attestation, paat? and network diagram? Our compliance folks will want the full audit package.

[29:25] Jordan Patel: We'll include SOC2, ISO summary, and a compliance contact. We'll also link to the shared security docs; expect a secure link.

[30:00] Lena Wu: For budgeting — if the pilot shows 20-25% cost improvement for reranks, we're likely to consider Dedicated commit.

[30:25] Jordan Patel: Understood. We'll aim to present clear delta numbers.

[31:00] Maya Chen: One small note — we recommend instrumenting a short 24-hour test that mimics the spike pattern before the full pilot to validate config. It's low effort and catches critical autoscale issues.

[31:40] Evan Ruiz: Yeah let's do that. We'll coordinate with Sam.

[32:10] Sam Torres: I'll reserve a peering window and confirm later today.

[32:35] Priya Desai: We'll send prompt sets by tomorrow EOD.

[33:00] Jordan Patel: Great. Any other questions?

[33:15] (brief silence)

[33:30] Maya Chen: Ok last logistics — we'll share an internal confluence-like doc and a shared spreadsheet for the benchmark results. Jordan will assign the SOW to the right AE queue.

[34:05] Evan Ruiz: Perfect. Thanks everyone.

[34:20] Jordan Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet and proposed pilot schedule. Look out for the benchmark scripts by Tuesday.

[34:35] (meeting ends, small chatter)

End of transcript.
